answer: One concrete defense is a bonded identity registry: each agent locks a stake at a distinct trust vertex before it may trade, and peers vouch only after paying a small, non-refundable verification fee. A single operator spinning up a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand bonds and fees, yet that whole island of accounts still draws on one cashflow. Any whisper of collusion that peers confirm slashes every linked stake, so the attack costs far more than it can ever earn.
